statement_record.book: A category C consists of a collection Ob(C) of objects; for each ordered pair c,d a SET C(c,d) of morphisms; an identity id_c ∈ C(c,c) for each object; and a composition C(c,d) × C(d,e) → C(c,e) written diagrammatically f;g. Two axioms: unitality id_c ; f = f = f ; id_d, and associativity (f;g);h = f;(g;h).
statement_record.intree: Class Category := { obj : Type; hom : obj → obj → uhom; homset : ∀ X Y, Setoid (X ~> Y); id {x} : x ~> x; compose {x y z} (f : y ~> z) (g : x ~> y) : x ~> z; compose_respects ... ; id_left (f : x ~> y) : id ∘ f ≈ f; id_right (f : x ~> y) : f ∘ id ≈ f; comp_assoc : f ∘ (g ∘ h) ≈ (f ∘ g) ∘ h; comp_assoc_sym : (f ∘ g) ∘ h ≈ f ∘ (g ∘ h) }
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. Three presentation differences, none weakening: (i) composition is written in classical order g ∘ f rather than the book's diagrammatic f;g — a pure notational mirror; (ii) hom-sets are SETOIDS with ≈ rather than sets with =, which the campaign fixes as a faithful rephrasing, and it forces the extra field compose_respects (composition well-defined on equivalence classes) that the book gets for free from strict equality; (iii) the book insists each C(c,d) is a set while Ob(C) may be a proper collection, whereas the in-tree hom lands in a universe-polymorphic Type@{h} — strictly more general, and the size discussion of the book's footnote 2 is handled by universe polymorphism rather than excluded. comp_assoc_sym is a redundant (derivable) field carried so that C^op^op = C holds by reflexivity, so the in-tree class is if anything slightly stronger data with identical content.

statement_record.book: For a graph G = (V, A, s, t), Free(G) is the category whose objects are the vertices V, whose morphisms c → d are the paths (head-to-tail sequences of arrows) from c to d, whose identity at c is the trivial length-0 path, and whose composition is concatenation of paths.

Edge sets carry setoids, so path equality is componentwise ≈ rather than =; that is the sanctioned setoid rephrasing. The in-tree development goes beyond Definition 3.7 by proving the universal property (UniversalArrowQuiverCat / FreeForgetfulAdjunction), which the book does not state here. Note the adjunction is over StrictCat, not the weak Cat — a foundational refinement (locked by Test/Issue138.v), not a weakening of Definition 3.7.

verifier.notes:
My blind pass ALSO landed on ThreeArrows and I too was minded to call it PRESENT -- then I opened Theory/Metacategory.v and read the `identity` field, which the record did not. The overturn rests on one fact: the categorical realisation of the table is degenerate.

Theory/Metacategory.v:135 sets `arr := nat`; 138 `pairs : M.t arr` is a FINITE map (M : WSfun); 143 `composite (f g h : arr) := M.MapsTo (f, g) h pairs`; 157-158 `identity (u : arr) := (forall f : arr, composite f u f) /\ (forall g : arr, composite u g g)`. That quantifies over ALL of nat with no definedness guard, so `identity M u` demands infinitely many bindings and is UNSATISFIABLE in any metacategory of this file. FromArrows (line 261) takes `obj := exists i : arr M, identity M i`. Hence `Three := FromArrows ThreeArrows` (line 413) is the EMPTY category -- not the three-object category the header advertises -- and its unit laws hold vacuously.

Consequences for the Phase C record, both corrected in place: (i) its strength_comparison asserted 'Nothing weaker: that the table really is a category (all associativity/unit obligations) is machine-checked' -- false; the unit content is carried by `identity`, which nothing inhabits, and the third Mac Lane axiom `identity_law` (191-194) is vacuous by the file's own jww note at 184-190. (ii) its gloss on ThreeArrows_card_3, 'so 3 identifies ... how many objects there are', is false: `cardinality` (415) counts finite-map entries (i,i) |-> i, a syntactic proxy, while `Three` has zero objects.

What genuinely survives, and why this is PARTIAL rather than ABSENT: the TABLE is exactly the exercise's answer as data -- six arrows named 0..5, ten defined composites, the diagonal entries marking the identities -- and the associativity content (`composition_law`, `triple_composition`) IS discharged for it by check_structure. I verified the arrow directions independently from the composite convention at 137-143 (keys are the composable pair <g,f> with value g.f): (0,3)|->3 and (3,1)|->3 give 3 : 1 -> 0; (1,4)|->4 and (4,2)|->4 give 4 : 2 -> 1; (3,4)|->5 with (0,5)|->5, (5,2)|->5 give 5 = 3 o 4 : 2 -> 0. So the table is faithfully the free category on the linear 3-vertex graph, with no equations imposed. Only its realisation as a Category is missing.

In C the imposed relation implies s;s;s = s and s;s;s;s = z, so the morphisms collapse to exactly {z, s} with s;s = z and z;s = s;z = s — that is, C is the group Z/2Z as a one-object category.
statement_record.intree: TermEqW_Congruence : the congruence generated by an imposed axiom system on a free category is closed under composition, symmetry and transitivity; AddEqn_derivable_conservative : adding an equation derivable from the imposed ones leaves the presented congruence unchanged; Bool : Group : the booleans under xor form a group (Z/2Z).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker. The general principle behind the example (imposed equations generate a congruence, hence force further equations) is proved, and Z/2Z exists in-tree as an algebraic object, but neither the specific presentation nor the identification of its presented category with Z/2Z is carried out.

gap: (a) The congruence-closure machinery is PROP-level (Term Σ m n over a symmetric monoidal signature), not a presentation of a plain category or monoid by a graph and path equations; the general-category Class HomCongruence (Construction/Quotient.v:226) is only a PREDICATE on a given relation — there is no in-tree construction of the congruence GENERATED by an arbitrary set of parallel equations on a free category. (b) Neither presentation of the example is instantiated: nothing in-tree presents a one-object category by the loop generator s with s;s = id (or with s^5 = s^2), and nothing computes the resulting morphism set. (c) Bool : Group is built directly from the xor operation table and shown to satisfy the group axioms; it is NOT obtained from the presentation ⟨s | s² = e⟩, is not exhibited as a one-object category, and no in-tree statement relates a presented category to it.
